AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: To describe the clinical presentation and treatment of a cat with flurbiprofen toxicosis due to topical cream exposure.

AbstractText.Label: CASE SUMMARY
AbstractText.content: A 3-year-old castrated male domestic shorthair cat presented to an emergency and referral center for acute lethargy, hematemesis, and anemia. Severe azotemia was observed on serum biochemistry panel. The patient's anemia was treated with packed RBC transfusion, and treatment with crystalloid fluids, famotidine, pantoprazole, ampicillin, and sucralfate were begun on presentation. Anemia became intractable and the patient received multiple packed RBC and whole blood transfusions. Severe gastric ulcerations and duodenal perforation were confirmed via gastroduodenoscopy, and the patient was treated with surgical excision and repair of duodenal perforation. Azotemia resolved with IV fluid therapy, and anemia resolved following surgery. The patient recovered and was discharged after 9 days of hospitalization. The patient had likely been exposed to the owner's compounded pain relief cream containing 10% flurbiprofen. There was confirmation of flurbiprofen exposure via acid extraction urine analysis at a university toxicology laboratory.

AbstractText.Label: NEW OR UNIQUE INFORMATION PROVIDED
AbstractText.content: This is the first described case of flurbiprofen toxicosis due to topical cream exposure in a cat.
